references.text: When Moses went up on Mount Sinai, the cloud covered the mountain, and the glory of the Lord rested on Mount Sinai. The cloud covered it for six days. This cloud as a sign of God's presence parallels the cloud that overshadowed the disciples at the Transfiguration.

The cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle. Moses could not enter the tent of meeting because the cloud rested over it. The glory-cloud of God that overshadows is a recurring theme linked to the cloud in the Transfiguration scene.

When the priests came out of the Holy Place, the cloud filled the house of the Lord. The priests could not stand and serve because of the cloud, for the glory of the Lord filled the house. God's presence manifested through the cloud creates awe and fear, just as the disciples were afraid when they entered the cloud.
Matthew's parallel account of the Transfiguration on the mountain, where a bright cloud overshadowed them and a voice sounded from the cloud. The disciples fell face down and were greatly afraid.
Mark's parallel account of the Transfiguration, where a cloud came and overshadowed them, and a voice sounded from the cloud.

On the morning of the third day, there was thunder and lightning and a thick cloud over the mountain. All the people in the camp trembled with fear. The fear of God's presence manifested through the cloud parallels the disciples' fear when they entered the cloud.

The people stood at the foot of the mountain, and the mountain burned with fire up to the sky, with darkness, clouds, and thick mist. God's presence in the cloud on the mountain is a theme repeated at the Transfiguration on the mountain.

The angel told Mary that the power of the Most High will overshadow her (ἐπισκιάσει). The same Greek verb is used for the cloud that overshadowed (ἐπεσκίαζεν) the disciples, linking God's power and presence in both events.

Peter himself testifies to the Transfiguration scene where they heard the voice from the exalted glory when they were with Jesus on the holy mountain. This confirms the event with the cloud and God's voice.
